overall: Atlanta experienced a significantly cooler-than-expected day on June 23, with persistent cloud cover (OVC conditions from roughly 08:52 through midday) and 0.74 inches of cumulative precipitation suppressing afternoon heating. The daily high of 73.9°F was recorded at 17:52 ET and, as of 21:30 ET, temperatures are declining (currently 71.6°F) with zero warming velocity — the day's maximum is almost certainly already locked in.
forecast_obs_notes: There is strong disagreement among NWP models: ECMWF (74.2°F) and HRRR (73.5°F) closely tracked observed conditions, while NBM (79.5°F) was a significant outlier to the warm side. The D1_PRIOR model badly missed with its peak probability in the 86–87°F range, reflecting a pre-precipitation baseline; the intraday model correctly homed in on the 72–73°F bucket at 94.6% confidence based on real-time observations.
max_temp_prediction: With the peak of 73.9°F recorded 3.6 hours ago, temperatures now falling, and the intraday model at 94.6% confidence in the 72–73°F bucket, today's TMAX is effectively confirmed at 73.9°F. The cloud cover, rainfall, and post-peak cooling trajectory leave virtually no scenario where temperatures could rebound to challenge or exceed this value tonight. Confidence is extremely high (>95%).
